source_span: On the week, IG cash widened just ~3bps, but ORCL Bonds & CDS moved +30-45bps wider... Capital hasn't disappeared. It's become far more discriminating... The question isn't whether investors still want credit risk. It's which risks they're willing to own, and at what price.
source_chain: IG100 closes only ~2-3bp wider while single credits (Oracle +43bp to +320, CDS +30-40bp, Meta +14bp, CoreWeave yields to 15%) blow out, therefore the index-level calm hides a market sorting issuers rather than fleeing credit broadly, therefore CoreWeave becomes the 'beta barometer' for how far that discrimination runs, with distressed/equity buyers only starting to appear late week; invalidation (Academy Securities, same week): the differentiation stays orderly only while dealer liquidity in new issues holds and CoreWeave doesn't break its July lows, and Academy sizes the downside risk (10-20bp IG/3-5pts HY) as bigger than any move tighter.
pulse_chain: Credit spreads on AI/hyperscaler debt hit YTD wides against a flat IG index (same Oracle/Meta/CDS/CoreWeave figures), therefore this is a sorting not a retreat: capital still wants credit risk but prices self-funding capacity vs. financing dependence (MS: AA+ hyperscalers at >30x interest coverage vs ~11x median IG are outside the squeeze; neoclouds funded on asset-level debt/converts are most exposed; CCC/HY data-center bonds already damaged), therefore Academy raises its alert from yellow to orange and sizes the escalation risk as bigger than any snapback tighter, while Goldman trades the differentiation (buy S&P ex-AI, expects Q3 ROI evidence); invalidation: CoreWeave testing its July lows, a break lower being next week's watch item, though distressed/equity buyers already showed up late in the week.
why: Every 'therefore' step, bank attribution, and the invalidation condition (CoreWeave's July-lows test, Academy's orange-alert sizing) match each cited note's own argument and direction with no reversal, no swapped invalidation, and no invented mechanism.
